name: abs
description: The `abs()` function returns the non‑negative magnitude of its argument, whether it’s an integer, float, complex number, or any object that defines an `__abs__` method.

name: aiter
description: aiter() returns an asynchronous iterator by invoking the __aiter__() method of an asynchronous iterable, providing a direct async equivalent of iter() without a two‑argument form.

name: all
description: The `all()` function returns True when every element in a given iterable evaluates as true (or when the iterable is empty), and False otherwise.

name: anext
description: `anext()` asynchronously obtains the next item from an async iterator (or returns a provided default if exhausted), mirroring the behavior of the built‑in `next()` but returning an awaitable that yields the value when awaited.

name: any
description: The any() function checks an iterable and returns True if at least one element evaluates as true, otherwise it returns False.

name: ascii
description: The ascii() function returns a printable representation of an object similar to repr(), but escapes any non‑ASCII characters using \\x, \\u, or \\U escape sequences.

name: bin
description: The bin() function converts an integer (or an object defining __index__) into its binary string representation, optionally prefixed with “0b”.

name: bool
description: The bool() function converts its argument (or defaults to False if omitted) into a Boolean value, returning True for any truthy input and False for falsy input.

name: breakpoint
description: It provides a convenient way to invoke the current debugger (by default pdb.set_trace()) at the call site, delegating to sys.breakpointhook() which can be customized or overridden.

name: bytearray
description: `bytearray()` creates a mutable sequence of byte values (integers 0–255), optionally initializing it from a string (with encoding), a length, a buffer, an iterable of integers, or leaving it empty.

name: bytes
description: The `bytes()` function creates an immutable sequence of 0‑255 integer values, converting the given iterable, string, or integer size into a bytes object that behaves like a read‑only version of a bytearray.

name: callable
description: The callable() function checks whether a given object can be invoked like a function, returning True for callables (including functions, methods, classes, and objects with a __call__ method) and False otherwise.

name: chr
description: chr() converts an integer Unicode code point (0–1,114,111) into the corresponding single‑character string, raising ValueError for out‑of‑range values.

name: classmethod
description: classmethod() converts a regular function into a method that receives the class itself as its first argument, allowing it to be invoked on the class or any of its instances.

name: compile
description: The compile() function transforms source code (as a string, bytes, or AST) into a code object—according to the specified mode, flags, and optimization level—so it can be executed with exec() or evaluated with eval().

name: complex
description: The `complex()` function converts a string or numeric input (or separate real and imaginary parts) into a Python complex number, handling parsing, type conversion, and fallback methods for custom objects.

name: delattr
description: delattr() removes a specified attribute from an object, given the object and the attribute name as a string, functioning like the statement “del object.attribute”.

name: dict
description: The `dict()` function creates and returns a new dictionary object, optionally initializing it with key‑value pairs from mappings, iterables of pairs, or keyword arguments.

name: dir
description: The dir() function returns a sorted list of the names of attributes accessible in the current local scope when called without arguments, or the appropriate attribute names for a given object—using its __dir__ method if present, otherwise gathering from its __dict__, type, and inheritance hierarchy.

name: divmod
description: The divmod() function takes two non‑complex numbers and returns a two‑element tuple containing their integer‑division quotient and the corresponding remainder, satisfying the relationship q * b + r ≈ a with r having the sign of b and |r| < |b|.

name: enumerate
description: enumerate() creates an iterator that yields pairs of a running index (starting at a given value, default 0) and each element from the given iterable.

name: eval
description: The eval() function parses and evaluates a given Python expression string or code object using optional global and local namespaces, returning the expression’s result while warning that executing untrusted code is insecure.

name: index-2
description: The `index-2()` function dynamically executes a given string or code object using Python’s `exec`, optionally with specified global and local namespaces, and always returns None.

name: filter
description: The filter() function creates an iterator yielding only those items from a given iterable that satisfy a provided function (or, if the function is None, that are truthy).

name: float
description: float() converts a given numeric value or appropriately formatted string into a floating‑point number, optionally using an object’s __float__ or __index__ method, and returns 0.0 when called without arguments.

name: index-4
description: The function `index-4()` converts a given value into a formatted string according to a format specification, defaulting to the standard `str()` representation when no format is provided, and raises a TypeError for unsupported or non‑string specifications.

name: frozenset
description: `frozenset()` creates an immutable set object, optionally initialized with elements from an iterable, allowing set operations without permitting modification of its contents.

name: getattr
description: `getattr()` returns the value of a specified attribute from an object, optionally providing a default value instead of raising an AttributeError when the attribute does not exist.

name: globals
description: globals() returns a dictionary representing the current module’s global namespace, reflecting the environment where the function was defined regardless of where it is later called.

name: hasattr
description: hasattr() checks whether a given object possesses an attribute with a specified name, returning True if it exists and False otherwise.

name: hash
description: The `hash()` function returns an integer hash value for an object, enabling fast key comparisons in dictionaries by ensuring equal objects (including numerically equal but differently typed ones) produce identical hashes, with the result truncated to the host machine’s word size for custom `__hash__` implementations.

name: help
description: The built-in help() function launches Python’s interactive documentation system, displaying information about modules, classes, functions, methods, keywords, or any object—either by starting the full help console when called without arguments or by printing a specific help page for the given name or object.

name: hex
description: The `hex()` function returns a string representing an integer’s value in lowercase hexadecimal notation, prefixed with “0x” (or “-0x” for negative numbers).

name: id
description: The `id()` function returns a unique integer representing an object's identity, which remains constant for that object during its lifetime (often its memory address in CPython).

name: input
description: The input() function optionally displays a prompt, reads a line from standard input, strips the trailing newline, returns the resulting string, and raises EOFError if end‑of‑file is encountered.

name: int
description: The int() function converts a numeric value or a suitably formatted string (or defaults to 0 when called without arguments) into an integer object, respecting optional base specifications, truncating floats toward zero, and using an object's __int__ or __index__ methods when present.

name: isinstance
description: `isinstance()` checks whether a given object is an instance of a specified type (or any type in a tuple or Union), returning True if it is and False otherwise.

name: issubclass
description: The `issubclass()` function returns True if the given class is a direct, indirect, or virtual subclass of the specified class or any class in a tuple or Union of classes (including the class itself), otherwise it raises a TypeError.

name: iter
description: The `iter()` function creates an iterator either from an iterable object (or sequence) when called with one argument, or from a callable that repeatedly produces values until a specified sentinel value is returned, at which point it stops.

name: len
description: The `len()` function returns the number of items in a sequence or collection, raising an OverflowError if the length exceeds `sys.maxsize`.

name: list
description: The built‑in `list()` creates a new mutable list object, converting an iterable (or producing an empty list when called with no arguments).

name: locals
description: `locals()` returns a mapping of the current local variable names to their values, reflecting the local symbol table for the current execution frame.

name: map
description: The `map()` function returns an iterator that applies a given function to each element of one or more iterables in parallel, yielding results until the shortest iterable is exhausted (or raising a ValueError if `strict=True` and any iterable ends early).

name: max
description: The max() function returns the greatest element from a single iterable or the greatest of multiple arguments, optionally using a key function for ordering and a default value for empty iterables.

name: memoryview
description: The `memoryview()` function creates a memoryview object that provides a zero-copy, sliceable, and mutable view of the underlying buffer of the given argument.

name: min
description: The min() function returns the smallest element from a single iterable or the smallest of multiple given arguments, optionally using a key function for ordering and a default value to return when the iterable is empty.

name: next
description: The `next()` function obtains the next element from an iterator by invoking its __next__() method, returning a provided default value if the iterator is exhausted instead of raising StopIteration.

name: object
description: The `object()` function creates a minimal, featureless instance of the ultimate base class from which all Python classes inherit, taking no arguments and lacking a `__dict__` so no arbitrary attributes can be added.

name: oct
description: The oct() function returns a string representation of an integer in octal notation, prefixed with “0o” (or “-0o” for negatives), requiring the argument to be an int or support __index__.

name: index-7
description: The function `index-7()` opens a specified file (or file descriptor) with given mode, buffering, encoding, and error handling options and returns the corresponding file object, raising an OSError if the operation fails.

name: ord
description: The ord() function returns the integer Unicode code point of a single-character string or the numeric byte value of a length‑1 bytes or bytearray object.

name: pow
description: The `pow()` function returns a number raised to a given exponent, optionally computing the result modulo a third argument more efficiently than using the exponentiation operator followed by a modulus.

name: print
description: The `print()` function outputs one or more objects as text to a specified stream (defaulting to standard output), separating them with a configurable separator, ending with a configurable terminator, and optionally flushing the stream.

name: property
description: `property()` creates a descriptor that lets you define custom getter, setter, and deleter functions for an attribute, optionally providing a docstring, enabling managed attribute access through attribute syntax.

name: property.getter
description: `property.getter()` returns a new property object that uses the specified method as the getter while preserving any existing setter and deleter functions.

name: property.setter
description: `property.setter()` defines a method that assigns a new value to a property, linking it to the corresponding getter so that attribute assignment invokes custom setter logic.

name: property.deleter
description: property.deleter() returns a new property object identical to the original but with its fdel accessor set to the decorated function, allowing deletion of the underlying attribute through the property.

name: property.__name__
description: It provides a mutable attribute that stores and allows retrieval of a property's name at runtime.

name: range
description: The `range()` function generates an immutable sequence of evenly spaced integers defined by a start, stop, and optional step, allowing efficient iteration without storing all values in memory.

name: repr
description: repr() returns a string that gives an official, unambiguous printable representation of an object, often one that can be passed to eval() to recreate the original value.

name: reversed
description: The `reversed()` function returns an iterator that yields the elements of a sequence or any object with a `__reversed__` method in the opposite order from their original arrangement.

name: round
description: The `round()` function returns a number rounded to a specified number of decimal places (or to the nearest integer if no precision is given), using “bankers rounding” where ties are resolved toward the nearest even value.

name: set
description: The set() function creates a new mutable set object, optionally initializing it with unique elements drawn from a provided iterable.

name: setattr
description: setattr(obj, name, value) assigns the given value to the attribute named by the string on the specified object, effectively performing the same operation as obj.name = value.

name: slice
description: The `slice()` function creates a slice object that encapsulates the start, stop, and step values (defaulting to None) for indexing sequences, enabling the same indexing behavior as the colon syntax and supporting use by built‑in and third‑party libraries.

name: slice.start
description: The `slice.start` attribute stores the starting index supplied when the slice object was created, serving as a read‑only value that other libraries (like NumPy) can reference but has no independent behavior.

name: sorted
description: The sorted() function returns a new list containing the elements of an iterable ordered according to optional key and reverse parameters, while preserving stability and leaving the original iterable unchanged.

name: staticmethod
description: staticmethod() converts a regular function into a static method that can be called on the class or its instances without receiving an implicit first argument.

name: str
description: The str() function converts any given object into its string representation, returning a plain text version of that object.

name: sum
description: The `sum()` function iteratively adds the elements of an iterable to an optional start value and returns the total.

name: super
description: super() returns a proxy that searches the method‑resolution order after a given class (or the current class when called with no arguments) to invoke inherited methods or access attributes, enabling explicit parent calls and cooperative multiple inheritance.

name: tuple
description: The tuple() function creates an immutable sequence object that stores a collection of ordered elements, allowing you to convert iterables into a fixed, indexable list-like structure.

name: type
description: The `type()` built‑in returns an object's type when called with one argument and dynamically creates a new class when called with three arguments (name, bases, and dict).

name: vars
description: vars() returns an object's attribute dictionary (or, when called without arguments, the current local symbol table) as a mutable mapping, raising TypeError if the object lacks a __dict__ attribute.

name: zip
description: zip() creates a lazy iterator that aggregates elements from each provided iterable into tuples, stopping at the shortest iterable unless strict=True is used to require equal lengths.

name: import__
description: The built‑in __import__() function is the low‑level operation invoked by the import statement that loads a module (optionally using globals, locals, a fromlist, and relative‑import level) and returns the top‑level package unless a non‑empty fromlist forces it to return the requested submodule.
